name: IC 10
tagline: The Local Group's starburst dwarf — the only one still erupting with star formation near Andromeda.

facts.label: Star formation
facts.value: Highest surface rate in the Local Group

history: IC 10 is the Local Group's only starburst galaxy — a small irregular near Andromeda where vigorous star formation is still blasting bubbles and superbubbles through its gas. It hosts Wolf-Rayet stars and X-ray binaries in unusual numbers for its size, evidence of a recent violent burst. Its proximity to M31 suggests it may have been captured and is now being reshaped by the giant.
